question.prompt: Three concentric circles have radii \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3.\) An equilateral triangle with side length \(s\) has one vertex on each circle. What is \(s^2?\)

solutions.title: Rotate through 60 degrees
solutions.explanation:
The radii satisfy \(1+2=3\), suggesting equality in a triangle inequality. A \(60^\circ\) rotation brings those three distances into one path.

Let \(O\) be the common center, and label the triangle so that
\[
OA=1,\qquad OB=2,\qquad OC=3.
\]
Rotate about \(A\) through \(60^\circ\) in the direction that sends \(B\) to \(C\), and let \(P\) be the image of \(O\). Rotation preserves distances, so
\[
AP=AO=1,\qquad CP=BO=2.
\]
Also, \(\angle OAP=60^\circ\), so \(AOP\) is equilateral and \(OP=1\).

Consequently,
\[
OC=3=OP+PC.
\]
A path through \(P\) has the same length as the straight segment \(OC\) only when \(P\) lies on that segment. Thus \(O,P,C\) are collinear, in that order.

Let \(H\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(A\) to the line \(OC\). Since \(AOP\) is equilateral, this altitude bisects \(OP\). Hence
\[
OH=\frac12,\qquad
AH^2=1^2-\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac34,
\qquad
CH=3-\frac12=\frac52.
\]
Applying the Pythagorean theorem to \(AHC\), we find
\[
s^2=AC^2=\left(\frac52\right)^2+\frac34
=\boxed{7}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

solutions.title: Subtract distance equations
solutions.explanation:
Squared-distance equations share the same quadratic terms, so subtracting them will locate the circle center in terms of \(s\).

Place the equilateral triangle at
\[
A=(0,0),\qquad B=(s,0),\qquad
C=\left(\frac s2,\frac{\sqrt3s}{2}\right),
\]
and let the common circle center be \(O=(u,v)\). The height of the triangle is \(\sqrt3s/2\), by the Pythagorean theorem.

The three radius conditions give
\[
\begin{aligned}
u^2+v^2&=1,\\
(u-s)^2+v^2&=4,\\
\left(u-\frac s2\right)^2+
\left(v-\frac{\sqrt3s}{2}\right)^2&=9.
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting the first equation from the second yields
\[
2su=s^2-3.
\]
Subtracting the first from the third yields
\[
su+\sqrt3sv=s^2-8.
\]
Since \(s>0\), these imply
\[
u=\frac{s^2-3}{2s},\qquad
v=\frac{s^2-13}{2\sqrt3s}.
\]
Substitute into \(u^2+v^2=1\), and write \(t=s^2>0\):
\[
\frac{(t-3)^2}{4t}+\frac{(t-13)^2}{12t}=1.
\]
Multiplication by \(12t\) gives
\[
3(t-3)^2+(t-13)^2=12t,
\]
so
\[
4t^2-56t+196=4(t-7)^2=0.
\]
Therefore \(s^2=t=\boxed{7}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
